title: Glide Alternatives: 8 Best Options Compared for 2026
summary: Jet Admin, Softr, Noloco, Stacker, Bubble, Adalo, FlutterFlow and AppSheet compared on data sources, permissions and real pricing. Checked September 2026.
body_markdown:
Glide turns a spreadsheet into something that looks like an app faster than anything else on the market. Teams leave when the spreadsheet stops being enough: the logic gets conditional, the data outgrows a sheet, or the per-user overages start showing up on a bill that was supposed to be simple.


This guide covers eight credible replacements and says plainly which fits which situation. Pricing was checked in September 2026.


> For governed internal tools and portals on a real database, Jet Admin. For the fastest Airtable portal, Softr. For Airtable-native portals with deeper roles, Noloco. For portals priced by customer count, Stacker. For a full product with custom UX, Bubble. For native mobile, Adalo or FlutterFlow. And if the company runs on Google Workspace, AppSheet.

## What is Glide, and why look for alternatives?


Glide builds mobile-friendly apps on Google Sheets, its own Glide Tables or a connected database. The learning curve is close to nothing, the output looks good on a phone, and for a field or internal app over data that already sits in a sheet it is genuinely hard to beat. Teams leave for four reasons.


### The logic outgrows what the builder can express


Conditional workflows, multi-step approvals and anything with branching get awkward. Glide optimises for the common case; the moment your process has exceptions, you are working against the tool.


### The spreadsheet becomes the bottleneck


A sheet has no real types, no relations worth the name, and permissions that belong to the file rather than the row. Airtable standard plans cap at 50,000 records per base. Nothing in the builder layer fixes any of that, and the migration costs more the longer the app has been live.


### Per-user overages arrive on top of the plan


Individual starts at $25 a month, Maker at $60, Business at $249, and users beyond the allowance cost $5 each per month. For an internal app that succeeds, the overage line is the one that grows.


### Permissions stop short of a real portal


Once external customers log in, the questions get specific: which rows may this partner see, which fields may this agent edit, and where is the audit trail. Glide handles simple row owners well and the harder version less well.


### When Glide is still the right choice


If the data fits comfortably in a sheet, the app is mostly lists, forms and detail views, and it is used by your own team on phones, Glide does this faster than everything else here.


## Types of Glide alternatives


The alternatives to Glide fall into five categories, and deciding which one you need removes most of the list before you compare a feature.


- Portal builders on a spreadsheet-style backend. The nearest swap. Softr, Noloco, Stacker.
- Governed platforms on your own data. The portal plus permissions and deployment. Jet Admin.
- Full app platforms. When it turned out to be a product. Bubble.
- Native mobile builders. When it needs to be in a store. Adalo, FlutterFlow.
- Ecosystem-bundled options. AppSheet inside Google Workspace.


## What to look for


Five things decide it. Where the data will live in two years, because that choice outlasts the builder. Whether permissions reach the row and the field or stop at the page. How external users are priced, since a portal cost grows with its success. Whether complex flows with several levels of related data are possible at all. And what the plan above the one you are quoting costs, because that is where the features you will need in six months usually sit.


## 1. Jet Admin, best for governed tools and portals on a real database


**Pros and cons.** Covers the same internal apps and portals but runs on the databases and APIs you already have, with permissions and deployment included rather than tiered. Not intended for public marketing sites or consumer products, and if your data genuinely lives in a sheet forever, a portal builder is less machinery.


**Key features.** Connects your own databases, warehouses and APIs with blending across sources. Granular component access, values passed between pages, server-side dynamic filtering for multi-tenancy, approval flows and conditionals without code, with JavaScript to extend. Figma import. Row and field level permissions, SSO, and cloud, self-hosted or on-premise deployment.


**Pricing.** Free plan with 20+ integrations and Figma import. Internal tools from $30 per user, client portals priced separately from internal seats.


**Best for** teams whose Glide app became a business system with real customer logins and rules about who sees what.


## 2. Softr, best for the fastest Airtable portal


**Pros and cons.** Faster than Glide for a read-mostly portal because it removes the canvas entirely. Same constraint means no multi-step flows, and API, CSV export and SQL connections sit on higher tiers.


**Key features.** Block-based portals and simple internal apps on Airtable, Google Sheets or a database, with member authentication and a large template library.


**Pricing.** Free plan with one published app and ten users. Basic $49 per month, Professional $139, Business $269.


**Best for** client portals that are lists, detail views and forms.


## 3. Noloco, best for Airtable-native portals with deeper roles


**Pros and cons.** More control over records, roles and workflows than Glide gives, in the same conceptual model. No free tier to try it on.


**Key features.** Portals on Airtable, HubSpot or a database with granular field and record permissions and workflow automation.


**Pricing.** From $49 per month, no free plan.


**Best for** teams who like the approach and simply need finer control over what each customer sees.


## 4. Stacker, best for portals priced by customer count


**Pros and cons.** Pricing maps to how many external people log in, which is fair until the customer count grows and the steps get steep.


**Key features.** Portals on Airtable and Salesforce with per-user and per-record permissions and a mature portal feature set.


**Pricing.** Personal $12 per month for 20 customers, Starter $65 for 100, Plus $129 for 200, Pro $249 for 1,000.


**Best for** client portals with a known and stable number of external users.


## 5. Bubble, best when it turned out to be a product


**Pros and cons.** The most customisable option here and the only one targeting public-facing SaaS. In exchange the app lives in a proprietary runtime, there is no code export at any price, and the bill tracks traffic.


**Key features.** Full visual development with its own database, workflow engine and plugin marketplace.


**Pricing.** Free for development, Starter $29-59 per month depending on track, Growth $119-209, Team $349-549, with overage at $0.30 per 1,000 workload units.


**Best for** teams whose Glide app was really the first version of something they intend to sell.


## 6. Adalo, best for simple consumer-style mobile apps


**Pros and cons.** A gentler path to a real mobile app than FlutterFlow, with the same weakness Glide has once data volume or logic grows.


**Key features.** Drag-and-drop mobile and web builder with its own collections, external API connections and app store publishing.


**Pricing.** Free for previewing only, Starter $45 per month, Professional $65.


**Best for** member, booking and directory apps where polish beats depth.


## 7. FlutterFlow, best for genuinely native mobile with code export


**Pros and cons.** Produces real Flutter applications for iOS and Android and hands you the source. Closer to development than no-code, and the backend is your responsibility and a separate bill.


**Key features.** Visual Flutter builder with Firebase and Supabase integration, custom code injection and full source export.


**Pricing.** Free tier, Basic $39 per month, Growth $80 for the first seat plus $55 per additional seat, Business $150.


**Best for** teams whose requirement is an app in the store rather than a web app on a phone.


## 8. AppSheet, best inside Google Workspace


**Pros and cons.** Cheap per user and deeply tied into Google, which settles it for many organisations before any feature comparison. The interface feels dated next to Glide.


**Key features.** Apps generated from Google Sheets, Cloud SQL or Excel with offline support, automation and Workspace admin controls.


**Pricing.** Free with limits, Starter $5 per user monthly, Core $10 per user monthly.


**Best for** business units already standardised on Google Workspace.


## Also worth knowing


Knack suits apps that are really a structured database with rules on top. Baserow and NocoDB are worth a look if the underlying problem is the spreadsheet rather than the builder, since both give you a real relational store you can host yourself. Airtable Interfaces covers simple internal views without leaving Airtable at all, which is often cheaper than a migration when only one view is missing.


## The question that decides this


Almost every team on this page is really choosing between two different projects. One is replacing the builder and keeping the spreadsheet, which is quick, cheap and buys you a year. The other is replacing the data layer, which is slower, more expensive and buys you the decade.


If you are already meeting record limits, permission limits or performance limits, the second project is the one you are actually in, and picking another spreadsheet-backed builder just resets the clock.
